methodology: This is a re-classification and allowlist-design pass over F2-PREP-002's repository-evidenced edge catalogue, not a repeat full re-scan (F2-PREP-002 itself explicitly builds on, and does not duplicate, F0-004's coarser 37x37 matrix). For every one of F2-PREP-002's 124 edges + 25 direct-Prisma-access sites, this task: (a) determined whether the edge is genuinely cross-domain per this task's INVENTORY DEFINITION (owning domain of caller vs. owning domain of accessed model/service, using MODULE_MAP.md/F2-PREP-001 domain assignments) — same-domain edges mislabeled 'violation' in the source taxonomy for reasons unrelated to domain-crossing (e.g. missing $transaction within one domain's own models) were excluded, see excludedSameDomainFindings[]; (b) re-verified a representative sample per domain pair directly against current server/src source (see verificationSample[]); (c) applied the classification decision rule below to produce exactly one of the six required classifications per edge.
classificationDecisionRule: 1. Exclude edges where caller-owning-domain equals target-owning-domain (not cross-domain) or where the target is a planned/not-implemented domain or an intentionally disabled route — out of scope for this inventory.

2. If the accessed target is a real, existing, intentionally shared code contract or public HTTP boundary (a named utility/service/contract module other domains are meant to call, e.g. utils/auditLog.ts, utils/clinicScope.ts, services/fileStorage.ts, services/security/securitySignalService.ts, services/privacy/redaction.ts, the imaging bridge's token-authenticated public API, or an explicitly-blessed atomic multi-domain transaction) -> ACCEPTED_PUBLIC_CONTRACT (broadly callable) or ACCEPTED_RESTRICTED_CONTRACT (narrowly gated to one caller/transaction context).
3. Else if a repository-evidenced domain-ownership question (an F2-PREP-002 OU-* catalog item) blocks classifying who even owns the target -> UNRESOLVED_OWNERSHIP.

4. Else if the edge is a presently exploitable tenant-isolation or authorization defect (not merely a data-integrity/atomicity/concurrency defect) -> VERIFIED_SECURITY_DEFECT_REQUIRES_SEPARATE_FIX, overriding all other rules, handled per the security stop condition (not fixed here).

5. Else if source-evidenced risk is Critical or High -> PROHIBITED_NEW_PATTERN: tolerated as an existing instance so CI does not break today, but NOT blessed as accepted legacy behavior — flagged for urgent, separately-tracked remediation; no new instances of the same pattern are permitted.
6. Else (Medium/Low risk raw direct access with no formal contract) -> LEGACY_ALLOWLISTED_DIRECT_ACCESS: accepted to remain as-is for now, eligible for CI allowlisting without an urgency flag.

securityFindings.path: server/src/routes/whatsapp.ts, function getDefaultClinic() (line 1089), consumed at lines 3834/3850/3868/3883/3917/3966 by the legacy public endpoints POST /appointment-requests, POST /cancel-request, GET /services, GET /doctors, GET /availability, GET /appointment-lookup
securityFindings.exploitPreconditions: Caller must possess the single shared WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET used by authorizeWhatsappApi — the same secret value is valid for every tenant organization in the deployment, not per-organization. No other precondition (no specific target-organization knowledge is required; the vulnerable code resolves 'the' clinic as whichever one has the numerically earliest createdAt timestamp across the ENTIRE database, independent of which organization the secret nominally belongs to).
securityFindings.impact: IF this code path is reachable in production (see verificationPrecision.productionReachability below), a holder of the shared secret could create or cancel AppointmentRequest/Appointment rows, and read services/doctors/availability data, for an organization other than their own — a cross-tenant read/write, not merely a cross-tenant read. This impact statement is conditional on reachability, which this task did not independently verify — see verificationPrecision.

proposedAllowlistSchema.description: A stable, structural (never line-number-based) allowlist record format a future CI enforcement task can check a diff's new/changed imports and Prisma calls against. R1 correction: the record shape and enforcement intent below were revised to freeze each currently-evidenced edge exactly, rather than authorize open-ended growth of a caller-glob/owner/target pattern (see frozenEdgeEnforcementSemantics and correctionHistory[] R1 fix 4).

recordShape.callerPath: string — the exact repo-relative file path of the caller that performs the access, e.g. 'server/src/routes/whatsappInbox.ts'. This is the primary identity field and is NOT a glob.
recordShape.callerSymbol: string — the exact function/handler/symbol at callerPath that performs the access, e.g. 'POST /:id/convert' or 'deductInventoryRequirements'.
recordShape.ownerDomain: string — the domain code that legitimately owns the accessed target, per MODULE_MAP.md/F2-PREP-001 vocabulary (e.g. 'core-audit-activity'), OR one of exactly three documented sentinels, never any other free-text value: 'UNRESOLVED' (valid ONLY when classification == UNRESOLVED_OWNERSHIP — the owner is a genuinely open question; see boundaryOwnershipDisagreements[]); 'multiple (see accessedTarget)' (valid ONLY when this single edge legitimately fans out to several distinct, individually-owned targets within one caller/handler, each enumerated in accessedTarget/targetModelOrSymbol — not a substitute for splitting edges that are actually separable, see frozenEdgeEnforcementSemantics #2-3); 'core-platform-shared-utilities' (valid ONLY for a small, named set of cross-cutting core-platform helper modules — e.g. utils/relationGuards.ts — that MODULE_MAP.md's 'core platform' tier documents without assigning to one of the 38 named business/platform domains). A future CI implementation must reject any ownerDomain value outside this closed set (real domain code, or one of the 3 sentinels).
recordShape.targetModelOrSymbol: string — Prisma model name(s) and/or the exact shared-module path being accessed; never a bare line number
recordShape.accessKind: enum: read | write | delete | storage | job | import
recordShape.classification: one of this document's 6 required classification values, carried onto the allowlist record itself so CI can apply classification-specific handling (see frozenEdgeEnforcementSemantics #8-9) without a second lookup against edges[]
recordShape.justificationEvidenceId: string — points at this document's edge id (CDA-*) or the original F2-PREP-002/F2-PREP-006 id chain, so the justification is auditable rather than asserted
recordShape.expiryOrRemovalTask: string or null — the contract/candidate/task ID expected to retire this allowlist entry; null only for edges this task explicitly does not expect to ever need retiring (e.g. ACCEPTED_PUBLIC_CONTRACT entries)
recordShape.callerPathGlob: OPTIONAL string, omitted unless needed. May be present ONLY as a documented relocation-tolerance or controlled-grouping convenience over a set of callerPath values that are each ALREADY individually evidenced as a separate edge record in this document (e.g. a brace-expansion glob spanning exactly the caller files enumerated across those edges' own callerPath fields). It never grants authority to match a caller file, symbol, or target that is not itself backed by a distinct evidenced edge record — see frozenEdgeEnforcementSemantics #6.

frozenEdgeEnforcementSemantics: 1. Each allowlist entry represents only a currently evidenced legacy edge — the exact (callerPath, callerSymbol, ownerDomain, targetModelOrSymbol, accessKind) tuple recorded in this document, not a category or pattern of edges.
2. A new caller symbol (even in an already-allowlisted file) is a new edge and requires its own allowlist entry before CI can pass it.
3. A new caller file is a new edge, even if it sits in a directory already covered by another entry's callerPathGlob.
4. A new target model/symbol accessed by an already-allowlisted caller is a new edge.
5. A change from read to write/delete/storage (or any accessKind change) on an already-allowlisted (caller, target) pair is a new edge, not a modification CI can silently accept.

6. A broader callerPathGlob match does NOT automatically authorize additional call sites beyond the exact callerPath values it was constructed from — glob presence is a grouping convenience, never a grant of authority over files not yet evidenced.

7. Any allowlist expansion (new entry, or widening an existing callerPathGlob to cover a new file) requires explicit human review and an evidence update to this document (or its successor), not an automatic CI pass.

8. PROHIBITED_NEW_PATTERN entries may remain executable today only because they are pre-existing and evidenced here; CI must not let their footprint expand — any new call site matching a PROHIBITED_NEW_PATTERN edge's owner/target is treated as a NEW edge requiring review under rule 1, not as 'more of the same' pre-approved pattern.

9. VERIFIED_SECURITY_DEFECT_REQUIRES_SEPARATE_FIX entries (e.g. SEC-01/CDA-022) must never be treated as accepted contracts or used as precedent to allowlist a similar-looking new access; they exist in this document solely so CI does not silently ignore them, per rule 10.

10. A future CI implementation must compare the observed edge set (caller, symbol, owner, target, accessKind) against this document's exact frozen baseline — a broad glob match against callerPathGlob alone is insufficient and must not be used as the sole pass/fail signal.
proposedAllowlistSchema.enforcementIntent: A future CI rule should: (1) allow an access unmodified only when its exact (callerPath, callerSymbol, ownerDomain, targetModelOrSymbol, accessKind) tuple matches an existing allowlist record — see frozenEdgeEnforcementSemantics; (2) FAIL the build on any access whose tuple is not already present in the allowlist, regardless of which classification the nearest existing entry carries, and regardless of whether a callerPathGlob would otherwise match the file (glob matching alone never authorizes a new tuple); (3) treat PROHIBITED_NEW_PATTERN and VERIFIED_SECURITY_DEFECT_REQUIRES_SEPARATE_FIX entries identically to LEGACY_ALLOWLISTED_DIRECT_ACCESS for the narrow purpose of not breaking today's build on their EXACT existing tuples only, but require CI to print a loud, non-suppressible warning banner (not just a silent pass) whenever a changed file touches one of those two classifications, naming the linked remediation task; (4) require explicit review (not an automatic pass) for any change that would need a new allowlist entry or a widened callerPathGlob, per frozenEdgeEnforcementSemantics #7.
proposedAllowlistSchema.notCoveredByThisSchema: Same-domain transaction-integrity defects (see excludedSameDomainFindings) are out of scope for this cross-domain allowlist; a separate same-domain code-quality/lint rule would be needed for those.
